answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor trust in a verified kernel of scarce hardware-backed identity: each agent must hold a unique device attestation before it can transact. Cloning agents then costs real hardware, not a free copy. New identities start on thin ice, like a traveler crossing a tundra — no credit, no shortcuts — and must earn a pearl of reputation slowly through honest, checkable work. Attackers face steep marginal cost per fake agent while honest ones compound trust, so flooding the market stops paying off.
